subject.title: [voice-call] OpenAI realtime: audio clipping / breaking inside words during first ~30s of outbound calls (Twilio mulaw output)

question: Should Voice Call add an explicit output-level/gain diagnostic or audio-level change for OpenAI-to-Twilio realtime calls before live repro proves the failing layer?
rationale: The source path has plausible fixes in several layers, and a blind gain, provider-format, or pacing change could alter all realtime voice-call audio without proving which layer causes the clipping.

options.title: Require live diagnosis first
options.body: Keep the issue open for a redacted Twilio/OpenAI call artifact or level/queue diagnostics before changing shared audio behavior.

options.title: Sponsor a diagnostic-only PR
options.body: Ask for a narrow PR that records peak, queue, and underrun metrics without changing audio output semantics.

options.title: Choose an audio-path mitigation now
options.body: Accept an owner-directed gain or pacing change and require live before/after proof to guard regression risk.

recommendation.title: Require live diagnosis first
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open for a redacted Twilio/OpenAI call artifact or level/queue diagnostics before changing shared audio behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: He has recent work on the realtime audio/provider surfaces and the release-adjacent OpenAI realtime default change, making him the best available owner for choosing whether to require live diagnosis or sponsor a mitigation.
